main_text.p: propositi syllogismi concludunt. Dici etiam poteft, argumento oppofitorum parium, feu vi confecutionis directae (quae graecis eft ἐπὶ πρῶτα ἀκολουθίας[?]) ob oppofitione factam per propria, propofitionis majores æquipollere his affirmatis: Qui perseverant ad finem us-que, salvi erunt: Qui habet Spiritum Christi, sunt ejus. Ita igitur syllogismi illi secundæ Figuræ dici poffunt, fed Modo deftituuntur, cùm conclufiones fint affirmatæ, non negatæ: proindeq; tantùm vi ac neceffitate materiæ concludunt. Facit ad hanc differtatiun-culam in vulgus etiam nota regula: Duæ ne-gationes reddunt fenfum affirmatum.
Ebrietas eft turpis. Audacia non eft ebrie-tas:Ergo audacia non eft turpis.
Nego confecutionem: quia in prima figu-ra assumptio non debet effe negata.
Ebrietas eft turpis. Ebrietas non eft auda-cia:Ergo audacia non eft turpis.
Nego confecutionem:quia in tertia figura affumptio non debet effe negata.
Si homo eft,animal eft.Sed eft animal:Ergo eft homo.

Nego confecutionem : quia hic connexus feu coditionalis nullius modi eft. In conftructivo enim non ponitur, id eft, affirmatè affumitur confequens, ut ponatur, id eft,affirmatè concludatur antecedens.Et reductus

page.notes: Greek at the end of the second paragraph: the word after "est" and the next word are hard to read at this scan resolution, so the Greek is marked [?]. The catchword "ad se-" is at the bottom right. The printed "assumptio" in the first syllogism line is written with a long-s ligature and follows "figu-ra", as printed. The running head is set in small capitals. The "ó" in "Goclenii" is printed with an accent; I have written it plainly as "Goclenii" because the accent is not clear. Stains and show-through at the page edges and foot are omitted.
